title: 第4章 虚无四第5章 虫世界
content_zh:
“你是我的妈妈吗？”呼喊妈妈的声音在病院里回荡，人影不停的晃动。
这个夜里终究是不平静的，这条街区的最边缘一道身影由破损的铁丝网下向外面钻了出去，正是拉曼，她一个人小心的在黑夜里向着目的地摸索前进。
她所要前往的地方那是一片撞击产生的坑，某样东西被防雨布盖住在那里。拉曼四周张望见没有看守的卫兵于是直接上前来到那东西跟前，伸手拉住防雨布的一角就要掀起。
“别动！举起手来！”突然的喝止声由身后响起，拉曼转身看去只见几名卫兵举着手中的蒸气枪正对着她的头向她示意。身为一名平民的拉曼根本没有办法反抗那些卫兵，她只能顺从的举起双手在两名卫兵的压制下送到了一旁的营帐里。
“长官，我们抓到一名奸细，她去那东西那里了。”卫兵将拉曼推进营帐一名身穿长官制服的男人就坐在那里。
“我不是奸细！我只是想看看那里面是什么。”拉曼用力的摇着头为自己的行为辩解，但是卫兵们显然不会听她的话，直接将她的手铐在了凳子上。
“你……”等拉曼靠近那个长官时她才发现这个男人的脸上已经开始有一丝丝的黑气由皮肤里冒出来了。
“不要！我不要呆在这里！”拉曼想要离开可是自己被按在凳子上根本无法逃离。
“如果你不想待在这里就不要进到这里！这里可是军事区域，不是你想来就来想走就走的！”男人怒吼，只是脸上写满了不舒服。
“你来这里是想要干什么？咳咳……我可不相信你只是好奇，咳咳。”男人不停的咳嗽，每咳嗽一下次就会有一丝黑气由身体里冒出来。
“听着，我要离开这里！我不是什么奸细，我只想来找我的孩子，那东西掉下来时我的孩子没有了，我想找到一点关于他留下来的痕迹也好，才来到这里的！我说了实话放我离开吧！真的！”拉曼看着那个男人神情激动的喊道。
“你们去看看她来的地方，也许不止她一个人。”那个长官向卫兵命令道。
“是的长官。”卫兵转身就离开了营帐。
“不要，放我离开！”拉曼用力的摇晃手铐可是没有人听她的。
“咳咳！咳咳！！”那个长官在卫兵离开后不停的在自己的位置上咳嗽，他感觉到自己越来越不好了。
“放我离开吧！我知道你会变成什么样子！现在只是咳嗽，可是马上你就会变得不是你自己了，我看过这样的事，所以放我离开吧！”拉曼向着那个不停咳嗽的长官乞求。
“你在说什么？我只是病了……咳咳……我只是……咳咳……”
“求你了！放我离开！”拉曼几乎是哭着央求着这个男人，可是他却无法做出别的事只是在那里不停的咳嗽，然后会有一股黑气放出。
“妈……妈妈……”一声妈妈开始由那个男人的嘴里发出来，他开始转变了。
街区边上隔着铁丝网作家望向了里面，营地里只有两名卫兵站在火堆那里发着呆。

“嗨！你好！我没有敌意，我只是想去见你们的长官！”作家由铁丝网外翻进来向着那两名发呆的卫兵走去，可是他们完全没有反应只是发呆。作家走到他们身后伸手拍了其中一个人的肩膀。
“嗨！听到我说话了吗？”作家问道，被作家碰到的那个卫兵转过身来看着作家的脸，用一种奇怪又熟悉的声调说：“你是我的……妈妈吗？”就在说完这句话的时候一股黑气升起替换了这个卫兵的脸变成了黑影，再去看另一名卫兵也是如此。
“这东西已经开始按捺不住向外扩散了，如果不去管那么这个世界的人类也许都会变成这种黑影。”作家望向另一边的营帐那里有熟悉的女声传出来。
“是拉曼。”
“睡吧，睡吧，我亲爱的宝贝……”温柔的女声唱出来的是那母亲独有的能安抚人心灵的催眠曲，那名本应化为黑影的营地长官现在正趴在桌子上好像睡着了一样一动不动。
“嗨。”作家的声音由门口传来，拉曼一边继续唱着一边回过头去看到了作家，但她向作家示意手上那被铐起来手铐说明自己无法离开的原因。
拉曼继续唱着催眠曲，作家小心的走过来将手指按在拉曼的手铐上，“盗窃者的信仰”随着作家的手指划动，手铐“卡”的一声轻响就被打开了。作家扶起拉曼慢慢向外退去，只留下那个看起来像是睡着一样的男人。
content_en:
"Are you my mother?" The voice calling for mother echoed in the hospital, and the figure kept shaking.
This night was not peaceful after all. A figure at the edge of the block slipped out from under the damaged barbed wire fence. It was Raman. She was carefully groping towards her destination in the dark night.
The place she was going to was a crater created by the impact, and something was covered there with a tarpaulin. Raman looked around and saw that there were no guards guarding him, so he stepped forward directly to the thing, reached out and grabbed a corner of the rainproof cloth to lift it up.
"Don't move! Put your hands up!" A sudden shout came from behind. Raman turned around and saw several guards holding up their steam guns and pointing at her head to signal her. As a civilian, Raman had no way to resist the guards. She could only raise her hands obediently and was suppressed by the two guards and sent to a nearby tent.
"Sir, we caught a spy. She went to that thing." The guard pushed Raman into the camp. A man wearing a commander's uniform was sitting there.
"I'm not a spy! I just want to see what's inside." Raman shook his head vigorously to defend his behavior, but the guards obviously would not listen to her and cuffed her hands to the stool.
"You..." When Raman got closer to the officer, she realized that the man's face had begun to have traces of black energy coming out of his skin.
"No! I don't want to stay here!" Raman wanted to leave, but he was pinned down on the stool and couldn't escape.
"If you don't want to stay here, don't come in here! This is a military area, you can't come and leave whenever you want!" the man roared, but his face was full of discomfort.
"What do you want to do here? Ahem...I don't believe you are just curious, ahem." The man kept coughing, and every time he coughed, a trace of black air would come out of his body.
"Listen, I want to leave here! I'm not a spy, I just want to find my child. My child was gone when that thing fell. I wanted to find some traces of what he left behind, so I came here! I told the truth, let me go! Really!" Raman shouted excitedly as he looked at the man.
"Go and see where she came from. Maybe she is not alone." The officer ordered the guard.
"Yes, sir." The guard turned and left the camp.
"No, let me go!" Raman shook the handcuffs vigorously, but no one listened to her.
"Cough! Cough!!" The officer kept coughing in his position after the guards left. He felt that he was getting worse and worse.
"Let me go! I know what you will become! You are just coughing now, but soon you will not be yourself. I have seen such things, so let me go!" Raman begged the officer who kept coughing.
"What are you talking about? I'm just sick...ahem...I'm just...ahem..."
"Please! Let me go!" Raman almost cried and begged the man, but he couldn't do anything else. He just kept coughing, and then a black gas would be released.
"Mom...Mom..." The sound of mother began to come out of the man's mouth, and he began to change.
The writer on the edge of the block looked inside through the barbed wire fence. There were only two guards in the camp standing by the fire in a daze.
"Hi! Hello! I'm not hostile, I just want to see your commander!" The writer walked through the barbed wire fence and walked towards the two dazed guards, but they didn't respond at all and were just in a daze. The writer walked up behind them and tapped one of them on the shoulder.
"Hi! Do you hear me?" the writer asked. The guard who was touched by the writer turned around and looked at the writer's face, speaking in a strange and familiar voice.Tiao said: "Are you my... mother?" Just after saying this, a black energy rose up and replaced the guard's face into a black shadow. The same was true when he looked at another guard.
"This thing has begun to spread uncontrollably. If left unchecked, then all humans in this world may turn into this kind of black shadow." The writer looked at the camp on the other side, where a familiar female voice came out.
"It's Raman."
"Sleep, sleep, my dear baby..." The gentle female voice sang the mother's unique lullaby that can soothe people's soul. The camp commander who should have turned into a black shadow is now lying on the table as motionless as if he is asleep.
"Hi." The writer's voice came from the door. As Raman continued to sing, she turned around and saw the writer, but she motioned to the writer that the handcuffs on her hands explained the reason why she could not leave.
Raman continued to sing the lullaby, and the writer carefully came over and pressed his fingers on Raman's handcuffs. "The Thief's Faith" followed the writer's fingers, and the handcuffs opened with a "click" sound. The writer helped Raman and slowly retreated outside, leaving only the man who seemed to be sleeping.
